title: Do graphs of maximum degree four have bounded slope number?
formal: Is there a universal constant C such that every finite graph of maximum degree at most four has a straight-line drawing using at most C edge slopes?
context:
Crossings are allowed, but vertices cannot lie in the interiors of nonincident edges. Planar slope number is a different parameter.

This question was found through Wikipedia and compared individually with the existing candidate and archived records. The linked literature provides definitions and background; this import is not a completed research-card review.
why: Locates a sharp transition in the geometric complexity of bounded-degree graphs.
